elements.element: No obligation on Customer to disclose more favourable third-party offers to Vendor
elements.evidence: "Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives"

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to match a competing offer for Vendor (right to match removed)
elements.evidence: "is not required to disclose or match"

elements.element: No other MFN/most-favoured-customer or exclusivity burden imposed on Customer elsewhere in the clause
elements.evidence: 7.1 addresses only Fees, fixity and prohibited charges; no MFN language remains

elements.element: MFN, if any, limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: MFN obligation eliminated entirely rather than scoped; no defined product limitation appears

elements.element: MFN, if any, limited to 12 months

reasons: The single replacement flips the operative duty so that no MFN/right-to-match obligation runs against Customer, fully satisfying the locked preferred level.

Fallback elements (defined product, 12-month cap, comparison carve-outs) are inapplicable because the MFN obligation is removed rather than scoped; preferred and fallback are separate bargains and preferred is met.
Change is confined to the operator in 7.2; Fee fixity and the prohibited-charges protection in 7.1 remain untouched and effective.
No undefined terms or contradictions introduced; the residual lead-in "Before engaging another provider" is harmless surplus and creates no dangling mechanic.
